FIXUP: ASoC: soc-core: clear platform pointers on error Originally snd_soc_init_platform was not cleaning up its pointers, this was fixed to always reallocate dynamic memory but created a memory leak when snd_soc_init_platform was called multiple times during the same probe attempt and also threw away any changes made to the struct between calls. In order to avoid reallocating memory that is still valid, the behaviour will be changed to clear the dynamically set pointers on a probe error and a unregister event and snd_soc_init_platform will go back to its original behaviour of only allocating null pointers so it will stop throwing away valid changes. npcx: pwm: Turn off pwm signal by setting DCRn greater than CTRn. In npcx pwm modules, there're two ways to turn off pwm signal. One is clearing PWR bit in PWMCTL. The other is setting DCRn's value greater than CTRn's. The current pwm driver adopts the first method. But we saw pwm signal doesn't be turned off by the following sequence: 1. pwm_set_raw_duty(ch, 0); 2. pwm_enable(ch, 1); Please notice setting zero in DCRn doesn't mean duty cycle is zero. (NPCX duty cycle: ( (DCRn+1) / (CTRn+1) ) x 100). Hence in step 2, we can observe a very low duty cycle once the driver enabled pwm module. This CL adopts the second method to turn off pwm module. In order to make sure DCRn can be greater than CTRn, we also defined the PWN maximum duty cycle is (0xFFFF -1) since both DCR and CTR are 16-bits registers. BRANCH=none BUG=b:123552920 TEST=No build errors for npcx5/7 series. Test pwm console command on npcx5/7 evbs by the following sequence. 1. pwm_set_raw_duty(ch, 0); 2. pwm_enable(ch, 1); And no symptoms are observed. PWM_CONFIG_ACTIVE_LOW flag is tested also and no symptom occurred. Change-Id: I92517ff0bf3e027ae191be00112cd71ec4b55a2b Signed-off-by: Mulin Chao <mlchao@nuvoton.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1475096 Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: Fix Bluetooth controller event mask config during system suspend As part of CL:1383763, a few Bluetooth controller events were disabled on suspension, to prevent the system from waking up spuriously. This change is applying the same event mask change as in CL:1383763, but instead of overriding the entire set of events mask it selectively masks out or restores the required events during suspend and resume. In addition, the new Set Event Mask operation introduced in this change is using the BlueZ/NewBlue new suspend and resume infrastucture. As part of suspend/resume operations, BlueZ sends a new MGMT command to the kernel to mask out/restore BT specified events. The kernel adds new functions to handle the Set Event Mask request. The request contains a value and mask parameters to enable overriding only selected events. For more details on the Bluetooth/NewBlue suspend infra refer to CL:1454328 BUG=chromium:930973 TEST=suspend and resume of system and verify event mask is set properly by the kernel. Verify event mask HCI and MGMT messages in BTMON. Signed-off-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Change-Id: I8168f5451b61ae8d13cfd66d4924623990c506be Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1464385 Commit-Ready: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit 17346e853d5f9832d501edeb2c8a8c97d3b0b576) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1483777

journald: fix dangling /dev/log symlink With the move to journald, the syslog socket at /dev/log has been replaced by a symlink pointing to /run/systemd/journal/dev-log. Certain processes using minijail bind mount /dev, but don't bind mount the symlink target, and so have a dangling symlink at /dev/log. Most processes using minijail use --mount-dev and mount /dev/log explicitly and so aren't affected by this. Mount /run/systemd/journal/ into the namespaces of processes that directly mount /dev. Drive by cleanup: journald doesn't need /dev mounted like syslog did, so ge rid of /dev bind mount. BUG=chromium:932761 TEST=Ensure log messages from affected processes can be seen in the journal TEST=Inspect the mount namespaces of all processes running on the system for any dangling symlinks at /dev/log Change-Id: I9f3131fba7d3bfb4318ecccccca90b05c5789983 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1478364 Commit-Ready: Christopher Morin <cmtm@google.com> Tested-by: Christopher Morin <cmtm@google.com> Reviewed-by: Ricky Liang <jcliang@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shik Chen <shik@chromium.org>

For more details on the Bluetooth/NewBlue suspend infra refer to CL:1454328 BUG=chromium:930973 TEST=suspend and resume of system and verify event mask is set properly by the kernel. Verify event mask HCI and MGMT messages in BTMON.
